entry.title: HTTP Semantics (RFC 9110)
entry.body: HTTP is a stateless application-level protocol for distributed, collaborative, hypertext information systems. A client sends request messages and a server responds with response messages. Safe methods are essentially read-only; GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE are defined to be safe. Idempotent methods have the same intended effect for multiple identical requests as for one request. PUT, DELETE, and all safe request methods are idempotent.

entry.title: JSON (RFC 8259)
entry.body: JSON is a text format for the serialization of structured data. It can represent four primitive types: strings, numbers, booleans, and null; and two structured types: objects and arrays. An object is an unordered collection of name/value pairs. An array is an ordered sequence of values. JSON text exchanged between systems that are not part of a closed ecosystem must be encoded using UTF-8.

entry.title: URI Generic Syntax (RFC 3986)
entry.body: A Uniform Resource Identifier is a compact sequence of characters that identifies an abstract or physical resource. The generic URI syntax consists of a hierarchical sequence of scheme, authority, path, query, and fragment components. The scheme and host are case-insensitive, while the path can be case-sensitive. Percent-encoding represents a data octet as a percent sign followed by two hexadecimal digits.

entry.title: WebSocket Protocol (RFC 6455)
entry.body: WebSocket enables two-way communication between a client running untrusted code in a controlled environment and a remote host. The opening handshake is intended to be compatible with HTTP-based server software and uses an Upgrade request. After a successful handshake, data is transferred in frames. Control frames include Close, Ping, and Pong. Clients must mask all frames that they send to the server.

entry.title: JSON Web Token (RFC 7519)
entry.body: A JSON Web Token is a compact, URL-safe means of representing claims to be transferred between two parties. The claims are encoded as a JSON object. The exp claim identifies the expiration time on or after which the token must not be accepted. The nbf claim identifies the time before which the token must not be accepted. The aud claim identifies the recipients that the token is intended for.

entry.title: TLS 1.3 (RFC 8446)
entry.body: TLS allows client and server applications to communicate over the Internet while preventing eavesdropping, tampering, and message forgery. TLS 1.3 removes static RSA and static Diffie-Hellman cipher suites; public-key based key exchange now provides forward secrecy. The handshake establishes shared keying material and authenticates peers. Zero round trip data has weaker security properties than other TLS data and is vulnerable to replay.

entry.title: QUIC Transport (RFC 9000)
entry.body: QUIC is a secure general-purpose transport protocol. It provides applications with flow-controlled streams for structured communication, low-latency connection establishment, and network path migration. QUIC uses UDP datagrams. Streams are ordered byte streams, but a loss on one stream does not prevent progress on other streams. Connection IDs allow connections to survive changes to endpoint addresses and ports.

entry.title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland — Down the Rabbit-Hole
entry.body: Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank. A White Rabbit with pink eyes ran close by her and took a watch out of its waistcoat-pocket. Alice followed the Rabbit down a large rabbit-hole. She found a little bottle labelled DRINK ME and later grew smaller after eating a cake marked EAT ME.

entry.title: Pride and Prejudice — Chapter 1
entry.body: It is a truth universally acknowledged that a single man in possession of a good fortune must be in want of a wife. Mr. Bingley has taken Netherfield Park. Mrs. Bennet is eager for Mr. Bennet to visit him because she hopes that one of their daughters might marry him. Mr. Bennet teases his wife before revealing that he has already visited Bingley.

entry.title: Vue.js Core README
entry.body: Vue is a progressive, incrementally-adoptable JavaScript framework for building UI on the web. The core library is focused on the view layer only. Vue is approachable, performant, and versatile. Development requires Node.js, and package management in the core repository uses pnpm.

entry.title: Express README
entry.body: Express is a fast, unopinionated, minimalist web framework for Node.js. Install it with npm install express. The repository includes executable examples and a test suite. Express applications can define routes such as app.get and start an HTTP server with app.listen.

entry.title: Qdrant README
entry.body: Qdrant is a vector similarity search engine and vector database. It provides a production-ready service with a convenient API to store, search, and manage points with an additional payload. Payload filtering supports business conditions alongside vector similarity. Qdrant is written in Rust and exposes HTTP and gRPC interfaces.
